newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PAPIN RETURNS TO SCENE OF FORMER GLORIES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PAPIN RETURNS TO SCENE OF FORMER GLORIES.

text.p: Jean-Pierre Papin makes a much
anticipated return to the Velodrome, the ground where he made
his name playing for Marseille in the late 1980s, with his new
team Bordeaux on Saturday.
Papin, back to the sort of form that once made him king of
French football, is set to lead the attack for third-placed
Bordeaux against Marseille in the French first division.
"I'll feel a sting in my heart but I'm avoiding putting
myself under pressure before (the match)," said Papin, who has
scored four goals this season for unbeaten Bordeaux.
Stories abound of both welcoming and unwelcoming receptions
for Papin from the fanatical Velodrome fans, many of whom will
not forgive him for his move to AC Milan in 1992.
A strong rivalry between the two clubs goes back to when
they were run by ambitious, controversial presidents, Bordeaux's
Claude Bez, now in prison, and Marseille's Bernard Tapie, who
was given a two-year suspended jail sentence in July for fraud.
Bordeaux's coach Rolland Courbis said: "Some (people) might
want the match to take place in the stands but I prefer it to be
played on the park."
Marseille coach Gerard Gili, whose side are plagued by
injuries -- including captain Jean-Philippe Durand -- and
suspensions, said: "There won't be an anti-Papin (tactical)
plan."
PSG defend their unbeaten record and a string of 10 clean
sheets, including two in the European Cup Winners' Cup, when
they travel to Guingamp on Sunday.
Second-placed Bastia could join PSG on 20 points for at
least 24 hours if they win at bottom club Nancy on Saturday.
Monaco and Metz, fourth and fifth respectively and France's
only survivors out of five teams in the first round of the UEFA
Cup, clash in the principality's Louis II stadium.
Champions Auxerre, buoyant after their European Cup
Champions' League victory over Rangers in Glasgow on Wednesday,
resume the defence of their French title at Montpellier, one of
France's UEFA Cup losers.
Reserve striker Thomas Deniud, two-goal hero in Glasgow,
keeps his place with the injured Lilian Laslandes now facing a
10-day recovery period after dental surgery on Friday.
